project.name: ccbot
project.description: Telegram Bot for monitoring Claude Code sessions. Control Claude Code sessions remotely via Telegram - monitor, interact, and manage AI coding sessions running in tmux. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: analyze_graph.py
nodes.summary: Analyzes knowledge-graph.json and produces hotspot/debt signals: per-file fan-in/fan-out, complexity, test coverage, layer stats, per-path scores and recommendations, written as report JSON plus markdown to the agentic output dir.

nodes.name: analyze_graph
nodes.summary: Core analysis: computes node/edge metrics, fan-in/out, filename-node, complexity and untested flags, per-path scores, layer statistics, hotspots and recommendations; returns a structured report dict.

nodes.name: _recommendations
nodes.summary: Builds human-readable recommendation strings from hotspots, untested files and complex files for the analysis report.

nodes.name: render_markdown
nodes.summary: Renders the analysis report dict into a markdown document (stats, layers, hotspots, untested, complex files, recommendations).

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point: resolves repo root, loads config and graph, runs analyze_graph, renders markdown, writes analyze.json and report.md to the output dir.

nodes.name: build_context_pack.py
nodes.summary: Builds a task-scoped subgraph slice (context pack) from knowledge-graph.json by seeding from a task's files/related nodes and BFS-walking the graph, then writes the pack JSON plus layers summary to the output dir.

nodes.name: _seed_ids
nodes.summary: Collects seed node ids from a task's related_nodes and file paths, including directory-prefix matches against file-type nodes.

nodes.name: build_context_pack
nodes.summary: Performs the BFS slice from seed id-s over graph edges, pruning by hop count, max nodes/edges; returns packed nodes, edges and layer stats for the task.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point resolving task by id, config and graph, invoking build_context_pack and writing pack.json/context-pack.md to the output dir.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the ccbot agentic pipeline wiring 16 subcommands (analyze, plan, select, context, status, list, validate, sync-issues, run, propose, show-import, reject, approve, request-changes, apply) through argparse to the shared pipeline modules.

nodes.name: cmd_run
nodes.summary: Runs the full pipeline: analyze, plan, render prompt, build context pack, optional validate and sync depending on flags.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Constructs the argparse parser with all pipeline subcommands and their options, including propose/HITL command registration.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Program entry: builds parser, dispatches to subcommand handler and exits with its return code.

nodes.name: mcp_server.py
nodes.summary: Stdio MCP server (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout) exposing the agentic pipeline (task list/get/select, analysis, context pack, implement prompt, status update, validate, status, analyze) as MCP tools with stdlib only.

nodes.name: tool_mark_task_status
nodes.summary: MCP tool wrapper around service.mark_task_status with status option validation.

nodes.name: tool_run_analyze
nodes.summary: MCP tool wrapper that runs the recommendation and pre-deployment validation for a task and returns the summary.

nodes.name: _handle_tools_call
nodes.summary: Routes received tools/call messages to the right tool handler and formats its result.

nodes.name: _dispatch
nodes.summary: Main JSON-RPC dispatcher: handles netiprocess to initialize, tools/call, tools/list methods and returns responses with ids.

nodes.name: _read_message
nodes.summary: Reads and parses one JSON-RPC message from stdin, including the spec-compatible Content-Length framing.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Server main loop: emits initialize confirmation then serves tools/list and tools/call requests until EOF.

nodes.name: paths.py

nodes.name: load_json

nodes.name: write_json

nodes.name: write_text

nodes.name: load_config
nodes.summary: Loads .agentic/config.json for the repo root.

nodes.name: out_dir
nodes.summary: Computes the agentic output directory from the config outputs.dir setting.

nodes.name: score_task

nodes.name: build_plan

nodes.name: render_plan_md

nodes.name: run

nodes.name: update_task_status

nodes.name: render_default_prompt

nodes.name: latest_proposal_dir

nodes.name: path_allowed

nodes.name: _write_temp_diff

nodes.name: build_proposal_md

nodes.name: cmd_reject
nodes.summary: reject subcommand handler.

nodes.name: cmd_approve

nodes.name: cmd_request_changes
nodes.summary: request-changes subcommand handler.

nodes.name: cmd_apply

nodes.summary: Registers propose-family subcommands on the CLI parser.

nodes.name: register_hitl_commands
nodes.summary: Registers HITL (show/import/reject/approve/request-changes/apply) subcommands on the CLI parser.

nodes.summary: Entry point: loads selected task, plan graph commit and templates, renders implement prompt + PR body and writes all outputs.

nodes.name: dumps_result

nodes.name: update_backlog_status.py
nodes.summary: Small CLI helper that updates a single backlog task status (with optional note) directly in .agentic/backlog/tasks.json.

nodes.name: _run

nodes.name: check_guardrails

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Central configuration: loads .env files and environment variables for token, allowed users, paths, transcript settings and display toggles; exposes ccbot_dir and permission checks.

nodes.name: auth.py

nodes.name: hook.py
nodes.summary: Claude Code hook integration: installs the ccbot hook into settings and, on SessionStart, records live session/window mapping into the session map file under flock with atomic JSON writes.

nodes.name: monitor_state.py
nodes.summary: Persistent monitoring state: tracks watched session transcripts (session id, file path, last byte offset) and saves/loads them atomically as JSON.

nodes.name: session.py
nodes.summary: Core SessionManager: manages window->session resolution, thread bindings, display names, group-chat routing, session map reads/writes with migration of legacy formats, and recent-message retrieval.

nodes.summary: PTB post_init hook: sets command list, resolves stale ids, constructs and starts the SessionMonitor, launches status polling async task and notifies handlers.

nodes.name: post_shutdown
nodes.summary: PTB post_shutdown hook: cancels status polling, shuts down message-queue workers, stops the monitor and closes the transcription client.

nodes.name: create_bot
nodes.summary: Builds the Application builder with token, rate limiter, post_init/post_shutdown hooks and registers command, callback-query and message handlers.

nodes.name: handle_new_message
nodes.summary: Delivers a new transcript message to all users bound to the session's window: switches/clears interactive UI, updates offsets, formats via response_builder and enqueues content/status messages.

nodes.name: _find_ccbot_path
nodes.summary: Locates the ccbot executable on PATH or in the active venv; returns path or empty string.

nodes.name: _is_hook_installed
nodes.summary: Checks the Claude Code settings JSON for an existing ccbot SessionStart hook entry.

nodes.name: _install_hook
nodes.summary: Writes/merges the ccbot command into settings' SessionStart hooks list and reports result.

nodes.name: hook_main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that parses hook input (/install flag or JSON payload), extracts session UUID and cwd, re-associates sessions and writes window->session map atomically under flock.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Singleton configuration object reading all environment/var values; provides is_user_allowed() and paths for state, session-map and Claude projects.

nodes.name: TrackedSession

nodes.name: MonitorState

nodes.name: WindowState

nodes.name: ClaudeSession
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a resolved Claude session: id, summary, message_count and transcript file path.

nodes.name: SessionManager
nodes.summary: Central session store: window->session via map + thread bindings, chat resolution, migrations of legacy formats, state-file persistence and helpers to fetch/recently read sessions.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads tracked-sessions JSON into MonitorState, rebuilding TrackedSession entries; creates empty state when missing or corrupt.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Serializes tracked sessions as dicts and atomically writes JSON, clearing the dirty flag.

nodes.name: _save_state
nodes.summary: Persists current window_states, user offsets, thread bindings and display names/group chat ids to the state file atomically.

nodes.name: _load_state
nodes.summary: Restores persisted maps from the state file and triggers legacy-state migration when needed.

nodes.name: resolve_stale_ids
nodes.summary: Lists live windows, computes stale session ids, applies startup migration and cleans leftover entries from the session map.

nodes.name: _migrate_old_format_map

nodes.name: override_session_map_entry
nodes.summary: Thread-safe override of a session-map entry via _mutate_session_map_locked.

nodes.name: _migrate_old_format_session_map_keys
nodes.summary: Applies legacy key-format migration to the session map file.

nodes.name: _cleanup_stale_session_map_entries
nodes.summary: Removes session-map entries whose window ids are stale vs live ids.

nodes.name: update_display_name
nodes.summary: Updates and persists the display name of a window.

nodes.name: set_group_chat_id
nodes.summary: Associates a user's group chat id with a window and saves state.

nodes.name: resolve_chat_id
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective chat id (group chat if present, else private user chat) for sending.

nodes.name: wait_for_session_map_entry
nodes.summary: Polls the session-map JSON up to a timeout waiting for a session entry for a window id to appear.

nodes.name: load_session_map
nodes.summary: Loads/validates the session-map JSON, lists live tmux windows, migrates/cleans stale entries and refreshes WindowState entries.

nodes.name: _get_session_direct
nodes.summary: Directly reads a ClaudeCode project transcript file: finds candidate session files for an id/cwd and parses recent messages via TranscriptParser.

nodes.name: list_sessions_for_directory
nodes.summary: Enumerates project session transcript files (from .claude/projects index or directory) and returns sorted ClaudeSession summaries.

nodes.name: resolve_session_for_window
nodes.summary: Resolves the ClaudeSession bound to a window, falling back through map/thread bindings and direct file lookup, and saves the binding.

nodes.name: update_user_window_offset
nodes.summary: Updates and persists the user's per-window view offset.

nodes.name: bind_thread
nodes.summary: Binds a user+thread to a window, saving and returning the window's display name.

nodes.name: unbind_thread

nodes.name: resolve_window_for_thread
nodes.summary: Resolves a user+thread to a bound window id.

nodes.name: iter_thread_bindings
nodes.summary: Yields (user_id, thread_id, window_id) for all bindings; falls back to legacy structure.

nodes.name: find_users_for_session
nodes.summary: Returns (user_id, thread_id) pairs subscribed to a given session id via binder/window states.

nodes.name: send_to_window

nodes.name: get_recent_messages
nodes.summary: Reads the tail of a session transcript with byte-range logic and returns parsed recent entries.

nodes.name: session_guard.py

nodes.name: session_migration.py
nodes.summary: Pure functions for migrating legacy persisted state: window-id detection, old name snapshots, startup state migration, session-map key format migration and stale-entry cleanup.

nodes.name: session_monitor.py
nodes.summary: Background session monitor: scans Claude project transcripts continuously, reads new lines via byte offsets, parses messages with TranscriptParser and emits NewMessage to a callback; cleans stale sessions.

nodes.name: transcribe.py
nodes.summary: Voice-message transcription via an OpenAI-compatible audio endpoint using a lazy httpx client.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Shared helpers: ccbot data directory, atomic JSON writes with stdout lock fd, and reading CWD from a transcript JSONL file.

nodes.name: is_user_allowed
nodes.summary: Delegates the permission check for a user id to the Config allow-list.

nodes.name: get_thread_id
nodes.summary: Extracts thread id from a Telegram update's message/callback; returns None for non-thread contexts.

nodes.summary: Builds a snapshot mapping each window id to its previous name before migration.

nodes.name: apply_startup_state_migration
nodes.summary: Re-attaches legacy state (session maps, bindings, offsets and names) to live windows by name and drops dead entries, returning StartupMigrationResult events.

nodes.summary: Converts old session-map keys (session id / cwd prefix) to the new indexed format, re-linking by live names.

nodes.name: cleanup_stale_session_map_entries
nodes.summary: Removes session-map entries that reference stale window ids, returning whether anything changed.

nodes.name: state_needs_legacy_migration

nodes.summary: Sends ogg voice data to the OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint and returns the recognized text.

nodes.summary: Closes the async transcription client if present.

nodes.name: ccbot_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the ccbot data directory from config/env, falling back to ~/.ccbot.

nodes.summary: Writes JSON via a temp file + os.replace to guarantee atomic persistence, preserving directory creation when required.

nodes.name: read_cwd_from_jsonl
nodes.summary: Parses the first 'cwd' occurring in a Claude transcript JSONL file and returns the working directory.

nodes.name: SessionContext
nodes.summary: Dataclass bundling (user, thread_id, window_id, window) that guards attach for downstream handlers.

nodes.name: StartupMigrationResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass returned by startup migration: new states, display names and human-readable event log.

nodes.name: SessionInfo
nodes.summary: Dataclass: session id + transcript file path found by scanning projects / index.

nodes.name: NewMessage
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a new parsed message event for the bot (text, role, content type, tool info, image data).

nodes.summary: Reads the current session-map JSON into a dict (id->window).

nodes.name: _cleanup_all_stale_sessions
nodes.summary: Removes tracked sessions not present in the current session map, purging offsets.

nodes.name: _detect_and_cleanup_changes

nodes.name: _handle_history

nodes.name: _handle_session_new

nodes.name: _handle_session_cancel

nodes.name: _handle_win_bind
nodes.summary: Binds an unbound tmux window to the thread: confirms mapping, notifies the window of its chat and flushes pending state.

nodes.name: _handle_win_new

nodes.name: _handle_win_cancel
nodes.summary: Cancels the window picker and clears pending-picker state.

nodes.name: callback_router.py
nodes.summary: Central, table-driven dispatcher: performs auth and group-chat capture, then routes every CB_* callback to a feature handler via exact and prefix route registries.

nodes.summary: Main entry point for all callback queries: requires the user, records the group chat, resolves and invokes the routed handler.

nodes.name: callback_screenshot.py

nodes.name: _handle_key
nodes.summary: Maps a kb: control key to tmux keys, sends them, waits briefly, and refreshes the screenshot in the message.

nodes.name: _clear_pending_thread

nodes.name: directory_browser.py

nodes.name: build_window_picker

nodes.name: build_directory_browser

nodes.name: build_session_picker
nodes.summary: Renders the session resume list with last-used timestamps and select/new/cancel rows.

nodes.name: screenshot_controls.py

nodes.name: build_screenshot_keyboard
nodes.summary: Builds the control-key row buttons for a given window id plus a refresh action.

nodes.name: errors.py

nodes.name: log_exception

nodes.name: reraise_retry_after

nodes.name: retry_after_seconds

nodes.name: capture_registry.py

nodes.name: CaptureTaskRegistry

nodes.name: cleanup.py

nodes.name: clear_topic_state

nodes.name: interactive_ui.py
nodes.summary: Mirrors Claude Code interactive terminal UIs (AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, permission prompts, checkpoint restore) into Telegram as live panes with inline-keyboard navigation, tracking interactive mode and message ids per user/thread.

nodes.name: get_interactive_window

nodes.name: set_interactive_mode

nodes.name: clear_interactive_mode
nodes.summary: Removes the interactive-mode binding for a user/thread once the UI is gone.

nodes.name: get_interactive_msg_id
nodes.summary: Returns the Telegram message id currently showing the interactive UI for a user/thread.

nodes.name: _build_interactive_keyboard
nodes.summary: Builds the inline keyboard for a window's interactive UI with navigation keys, actions, Enter, and Question-mark help entries.

nodes.name: handle_interactive_ui
nodes.summary: Captures the tmux pane, detects and renders the interactive UI content with an inline keyboard, edits or sends the Telegram message, and deletes it when UI disappears.

nodes.name: clear_interactive_msg

nodes.name: message_handlers.py
nodes.summary: Telegram message handlers for text, photo, and voice notes plus streaming '!' bash command capture; routes user input into the bound Claude Code tmux window or the window/session pickers.

nodes.name: photo_handler
nodes.summary: Downloads an incoming photo into the images directory and sends its path to the bound Claude Code window so it can be processed.

nodes.name: voice_handler
nodes.summary: Downloads a voice message, transcribes it via OpenAI, and sends the transcription text to the session window.

nodes.name: cancel_bash_capture
nodes.summary: Cancels any running bash output capture task for a user/thread via the capture registry.

nodes.name: capture_bash_output
nodes.summary: Polls the tmux pane for '!' bash command output, converts markdown, and edits the result into a Telegram message while streaming progress.

nodes.name: text_handler
nodes.summary: Primary text dispatcher: enforces guards, binds sessions, drives window/directory/session pickers, starts bash captures, routes to interactive UI handling, or sends text to the bound window.

nodes.name: message_queue.py
nodes.summary: Per-user message queue system providing FIFO-ordered delivery, status messages that always follow content, consecutive task merging, per-thread task routing, and flood control managed by a process-wide queue manager.

nodes.name: MessageTask
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a queued message task: task type, text, parts, tool_use_id, content_type, optional thread_id, and embedded image data.

nodes.name: StatusTracker
nodes.summary: Per-topic tracker of the latest status text and tool_use -> message-id map with set/get/pop operations and topic-wide clearing.

nodes.name: MessageQueueManager
nodes.summary: Process-wide manager owning per-user queues, worker tasks, per-user locks, flood-control timestamps, and shutdown orchestration.

nodes.name: get_message_queue
nodes.summary: Returns the existing queue for a user, or None if it has not been created yet.

nodes.name: get_or_create_queue
nodes.summary: Creates a user's queue and its background worker task if missing, otherwise returns the existing queue.

nodes.name: clear_status_msg_info
nodes.summary: Clears the tracked status message id for a topic.

nodes.name: clear_tool_msg_ids_for_topic
nodes.summary: Clears the tool_use -> message-id tracking entries for a topic.

nodes.name: shutdown_workers
nodes.summary: Shuts down all message queues, worker tasks, and tracked state globally.

nodes.name: _inspect_queue
nodes.summary: Snapshots a queue's pending tasks without consuming them, for merge decisions.

nodes.name: _can_merge_tasks
nodes.summary: Checks whether two consecutive content tasks are mergeable (compatible topic/tool and within size budget).

nodes.name: _merge_content_tasks
nodes.summary: Walks the queue, merging consecutive compatible content tasks into a single message within the length ceiling, preserving the original edit strategy.

nodes.name: _process_content_with_retry
nodes.summary: Attempts to send the dequeue content task with RetryAfter-aware retries and flood-control accounting.

nodes.name: _message_queue_worker
nodes.summary: Per-user background loop pulling tasks FIFO: merges consecutive content, dispatches to content/status handlers, applies flood waits, and logs failures without crashing.

nodes.name: _send_task_images
nodes.summary: Sends any attached image data from a message task via send_photo.

nodes.name: _process_content_task
nodes.summary: Delivers a content task: edits the existing tool message, sends new messages with fallback, sends attached images, and refreshes status afterwards.

nodes.name: _convert_status_to_content
nodes.summary: When content arrives in place of a pending status message, deletes the status message and edits content into the release tool's message.

nodes.name: _process_status_update_task
nodes.summary: Applies a status update task: edit or replace the tracked status message respecting send/clear ordering and typing.

nodes.name: _do_send_status_message
nodes.summary: Sends a status message with chat-action typing, storing the resulting message id in the tracker for later edits or clears.

nodes.name: _do_clear_status_message
nodes.summary: Deletes the tracked status message for a topic when present, resilient to stale messages.

nodes.name: _check_and_send_status
nodes.summary: When the queue is idle and the pane shows active working text, synthesizes and sends a one-shot status update for the topic.

nodes.name: enqueue_content_message
nodes.summary: Enqueues a content message task for the user, creating the queue and worker if absent.

nodes.name: enqueue_status_update
nodes.summary: Enqueues a status update with alias/merge handling so statuses follow content; skips redundant updates when flooded.

nodes.name: status_polling.py
nodes.summary: Background polling subsystem for thread-bound windows: detects Claude Code status lines and interactive UIs, enqueues status updates, and cleans up deleted windows and topics.

nodes.name: update_status_message
nodes.summary: Captures a window's pane, classifies status vs interactive UI content, cleans stale interactive messages, and enqueues the resulting status update.

nodes.name: status_poll_loop
nodes.summary: Main loop iterating thread bindings every second: detects released/empty windows, kills missing ones, unbinds stale topics, probes topic existence, and refreshes status messages.

nodes.name: terminal_parser.py
nodes.summary: Regex-based parser for Claude Code tmux pane text: detects interactive UIs (delimiter patterns), status lines by spinner scan, bash output, and usage output; centralizes all Claude text patterns.
nodes.languageNotes: All Claude Code text patterns centralized in UI_PATTERNS and STATUS_SPINNERS constants.

nodes.name: InteractiveUIContent
nodes.summary: Dataclass carrying an extracted interactive UI's content text and UI-name.

nodes.name: UIPattern
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a UI layout: name, top and bottom delimiter regexes, and minimum vertical gap between them.

nodes.name: _shorten_separators
nodes.summary: Collapses long runs of dash separators in extracted UI text.

nodes.name: _try_extract
nodes.summary: Searches pane lines for a UI's top/bottom delimiter pattern and returns the inner content slice, or None.

nodes.name: extract_interactive_content
nodes.summary: Detects matching known interactive UI patterns in pane text and returns structured content.

nodes.name: is_interactive_ui
nodes.summary: Boolean convenience check whether the pane text contains interactive UI content.

nodes.name: parse_status_line
nodes.summary: Bottom-up scan of pane lines to locate the spinner + working text line that represents Claude Code's current status.

nodes.name: strip_pane_chrome
nodes.summary: Removes tmux bottom bar / prompt chrome lines from captured output.

nodes.name: extract_bash_output
nodes.summary: Extracts the output printed after a bash command prompt, dropping the trailing shell prompt and duplicate tail lines.

nodes.name: UsageInfo
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding the raw usage pane text plus the cleaned parsed lines.

nodes.name: parse_usage_output
nodes.summary: Parses Claude Code's usage pane output into cleaned lines and a UsageInfo value, stripping unicode half-block characters.

nodes.name: tmux_manager.py
nodes.summary: Async-friendly wrapper around libtmux managing a single tmux session for Claude Code windows: list/find/create/kill/rename windows, capture panes, send keys and control sequences, with sensitive-env scrubbing.
nodes.languageNotes: All blocking libtmux calls are offloaded via asyncio.to_thread so the event loop never blocks.

nodes.name: TmuxWindow
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a discovered tmux window: id, name, working directory, and active pane command.

nodes.name: TmuxManager
nodes.summary: Singleton exposing everything the bot needs from tmux: session bootstrap with env scrubbing, window discovery, pane capture, key sending, renaming, killing, and Claude Code window creation in a work directory.

nodes.name: command_handlers.py
nodes.summary: Telegram command handlers and forum lifecycle callbacks: /start, /history, /screenshot, /unbind, /esc, /usage and /forward commands, plus topic_closed / topic_edited handlers that kill or rename the bound tmux window, and a fallback for unsupported content.

nodes.name: start_command
nodes.summary: Sends the welcome menu to authorized users, clearing any leftover window-picker/browse state; refuses unauthorized users.

nodes.name: history_command
nodes.summary: Checks the thread is bound to a window and then delegates transcript delivery to send_history.

nodes.name: screenshot_command
nodes.summary: Captures and renders the bound tmux pane as an image (with ANSI styling), then sends it as a document plus a screenshot refresh keyboard.

nodes.name: unbind_command
nodes.summary: Unbinds the current thread from its tmux window: requires the topic, resolves the window display name, unbinds the thread, clears topic state and replies.

nodes.name: esc_command
nodes.summary: Sends an ESC key sequence to the bound window's tmux pane to cancel Claude's current input.

nodes.name: usage_command
nodes.summary: Injects /usage into the pane, waits, captures it, parses the usage modal and replies with the parsed cost output or an error.

nodes.name: topic_closed_handler
nodes.summary: ForumTopicClosed event handler: kills the tmux window bound to the closed topic and unbinds the thread, or only unbinds when the window is shared in another group.

nodes.name: topic_edited_handler
nodes.summary: ForumTopicEdited handler that renames the bound tmux window and updates the persisted display name when the topic title changes.

nodes.name: forward_command_handler
nodes.summary: /forward command: forwards text or a /cc slash command to another bound session's window, re-binding the group chat as needed; also supports /forward ... reset via the unset branch.

nodes.name: unsupported_content_handler
nodes.summary: Fallback that replies when a message contains content the bot cannot process (e.g., stickers/animation) after authorization.

nodes.name: history.py
nodes.summary: Transcript history delivery for Telegram topics: builds paginated reply keyboards, formats the window's JSONL history into display chunks with byte-range slicing, and sends/edits them under Telegram message-size limits.

nodes.name: _build_history_keyboard
nodes.summary: Builds the inline pagination keyboard for a history page: new-page, prev/next page and back buttons, each with safe_callback_data payloads.

nodes.name: send_history
nodes.summary: Fetches the bound window's recent messages, groups them by timestamp into pages with byte range slicing, renders them, and sends or edits the page with the pagination keyboard.

nodes.name: message_sender.py
nodes.summary: Robust Telegram outgoing-message layer: singleton MessageFormatter renders content as Telegram MarkdownV2 or plain text, and send/edit/photo helpers with plain-text fallback on BadRequest, sentinel stripping, and comment-aware repr.
nodes.languageNotes: Built on python-telegram-bot; send_photo inspects image bytes to decide between send_photo and send_media_group.

nodes.name: strip_sentinels
nodes.summary: Removes sentinel token markers the bot injects around plain content so fallback plain text stays clean.

nodes.name: MessageFormatter
nodes.summary: Singleton formatter that renders content to Telegram MarkdownV2 via convert_markdown or to stripped plain text, exposing both to_markdown_v2 and to_plain for fallback logic.

nodes.name: _run_markdown_fallback
nodes.summary: Attempts a markdown operation and falls back to the plain-text operation on BadRequest, logging context (function, type) for observability.

nodes.name: send_with_fallback
nodes.summary: Public send helper: posts a message with MarkdownV2, retries once with plain text on parse failure, and re-raises RetryAfter-worthy errors.

nodes.name: edit_with_fallback
nodes.summary: Edits an existing message's text with MarkdownV2 and falls back to plain, used for streaming updates and photo captions.

nodes.name: send_photo
nodes.summary: Sends image bytes as a photo or as an InputMediaPhoto group when the frame is large, honoring the thread id; logs failures with the exception type and returns the result.

nodes.name: safe_reply
nodes.summary: Replies to a Telegram message with MarkdownV2, falling back to plain text; propagates retry-after errors and re-asks caller-specific fallback.

nodes.name: safe_edit
nodes.summary: Edits a message with MarkdownV2 + plain-text fallback, reusing the shared fallback runner used by safe_reply.

nodes.name: safe_send
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that delegates to send_with_fallback for sending content messages to a chat.

nodes.name: response_builder.py
nodes.summary: Splits a Claude response into Telegram-safe parts: converts markdown tables, strips the expanded card headers and splits long text into chunked content parts.

nodes.name: build_response_parts
nodes.summary: Converts tables, strips the line-join epilogue, splits the text with split_message, and emits a list of content parts (and optional image parts) for the queue.

nodes.name: markdown_v2.py
nodes.summary: Markdown-to-Telegram-MarkdownV2 converter: converts tables into expandable card blocks, escapes reserved characters, renders expandable quote regions, and renders the remaining markdown to MarkdownV2 with a mistletoe-based renderer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses mistletoe's TelegramMarkdownRenderer plus regex passes for tables and expandable quotes; kept as pure string-in/string-out helpers.

nodes.name: _split_table_row
nodes.summary: Splits a markdown table row on unescaped pipes and strips cell whitespace for rendering.

nodes.name: convert_markdown_tables
nodes.summary: Detects header/separator/data row tables and converts each into a compact expandable card block so Telegram renders tables cleanly.

nodes.name: _escape_mdv2
nodes.summary: Escapes reserved Telegram MarkdownV2 characters (_, *, [, ], etc.) in text.

nodes.name: _render_expandable_quote
nodes.summary: Builds the Telegram blockquote 'expandable' block from matched quote content, splitting long content into collapsible blocks.

nodes.name: _markdownify
nodes.summary: Renders a markdown document to MarkdownV2 via the TelegramMarkdownRenderer, after token/syntax cleanup passes.

nodes.name: convert_markdown
nodes.summary: Main entry point: converts tables to expandable blocks, renders expandable quotes, and renders the rest to MarkdownV2, returning a Telegram-safe string.

nodes.name: screenshot.py
nodes.summary: Renders terminal text (with ANSI styles) into PNG images with Pillow for Telegram screenshots: font tiering for CJK, ANSI SGR parsing, 256-color approximation, and async image rendering.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Pillow (ImageFont, ImageDraw); renders in an asyncio.to_thread worker via text_to_image.

nodes.name: TextStyle
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing foreground/background colors of a styled text run.

nodes.name: StyledSegment
nodes.summary: Dataclass pairing text with its TextStyle and font tier used during image layout.

nodes.name: _load_font
nodes.summary: Loads a TrueType font at a given size, falling back to Pillow's default font with a warning on failure.

nodes.name: _font_tier
nodes.summary: Classifies a character into a font tier (CJK vs base) based on code point ranges to choose the correct font.

nodes.name: _parse_ansi_line
nodes.summary: Parses a terminal line with ANSI SGR escapes into styled segments, applying per-pane text splitting for wide characters.

nodes.name: _apply_ansi_codes
nodes.summary: Maps ANSI SGR codes (fg/bg, 256-color, bright) onto a TextStyle, approximating 256-color indices to RGB.

nodes.name: _approximate_256_color
nodes.summary: Converts a 256-index color cube code into an approximated (r, g, b) tuple.

nodes.name: _split_line_segments_plain
nodes.summary: Splits an un-ANSI line into font-tier segments so CJK and base glyphs render at correct widths.

nodes.name: text_to_image
nodes.summary: Async entry point: measures and rasterizes styled line segments onto a Pillow image honoring ANSI colors and wide chars, returns PNG bytes.

nodes.name: telegram_sender.py
nodes.summary: Message length utilities: UTF-16 length calculation (Telegram's counting), forced splitting of over-long lines, and code-block-aware split_message for the 4096-char message limit.

nodes.name: utf16_len
nodes.summary: Returns the UTF-16 code unit length of text, matching Telegram's counting for message limits.

nodes.name: _force_split
nodes.summary: Splits a single over-budget line into code unit exact chunks, preserving wide UTF-16 pairs.

nodes.name: split_message
nodes.summary: Chunks a message into up-to-max_length parts while keeping code fences and line boundaries intact, fusing small lines into blocks.

nodes.name: transcript_parser.py
nodes.summary: Parses Claude Code JSONL session transcripts for Telegram: classifies message types, extracts text and tool results (with images), renders tool-use summaries and edit diffs, and formats expandable quotes for chat display.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure parser driven by regex and JSONL block shape; produces ParsedEntry lists consumed by session_monitor.

nodes.name: ParsedMessage
nodes.summary: Lightweight model of a single parsed transcript message: message_type and optional text/tool_name attributes.

nodes.name: ParsedEntry
nodes.summary: A user-message entry: role, formatted text, content type, tool use/results ids, timestamp; carries image data when applicable.

nodes.name: PendingToolInfo
nodes.summary: Bookkeeping record for a tool_use awaiting its tool_result (summary, tool name, input data).

nodes.name: TranscriptParser
nodes.summary: Main parser: parse_line classification, extract_text_only, format_tool_use_summary, tool result text/image extraction, and parse_entries building ParsedEntry lists from transcript JSONL with pending tool tracking.

nodes.name: .github/workflows/agentic-analyze.yml

nodes.name: .github/workflows/agentic-implement.yml

nodes.name: .github/workflows/check.yml

nodes.name: .github/workflows/claude.yml

nodes.name: HANDOFF_REF-006.md

nodes.name: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Full executable plan for the ccbot agentic pipeline: automates knowledge-graph + refactoring backlog into ranked atomic tasks, Grok-enriched plan/review, implement prompt, quality gates and mandatory human merge. nodes.name: README.md

nodes.name: config.json

nodes.name: analyze.md

nodes.name: plan.md

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what ccbot is: a thin Telegram control layer over Claude Code sessions running in tmux. It explains the one-session-per-tmux-window model, how Telegram topics map to sessions, and the full feature list (monitor, interact, manage).
tour.languageLesson: ccbot is an 'external control plane' rather than an in-process plugin: it never runs inside Claude Code's process, it simply types keys into tmux panes and reads their output. This boundary keeps it safe Р Р†Р вЂљРІР‚Сњ even if the bot crashes, the AI session keeps running.

tour.title: Packaging & Configuration
tour.description: See how the project is built (pyproject.toml, Python 3.12, python-telegram-bot + libtmux) and what it needs to run. The .env.example template lists every environment variable, and config.py loads and validates them centrally.
tour.languageLesson: 12-factor config: all settings come from environment variables with .env-file support. config.py is a thin facade Р Р†Р вЂљРІР‚Сњ every other module reads tokens, paths and permission policy from it, which is why it ranks near the top of the fan-in table (widely depended upon, low change surface).

tour.title: Entry Point & Application Wiring
tour.description: main.py is the CLI entrypoint; bot.py builds the python-telegram-bot Application, registers every command/message/callback handler, and starts the session monitor, status-poll loop and message-queue workers. This is the hub everything else plugs into (top fan-out).
tour.languageLesson: Fan-out vs fan-in: bot.py is a fan-out hub (it reaches out to dozens of handlers), while session.py/tmux_manager.py are fan-in sinks (dozens of modules depend on them). When exploring a codebase, fan-in reveals the load-bearing foundation, fan-out reveals the integration surface.

tour.title: Architecture Rules & Feature Map
tour.description: document:doc/telegram-bot-features.md inventories every feature; .claude/rules/architecture.md codifies the invariants that keep the design coherent (session/topic mapping, message-handling, topic architecture). Read the rules before touching code Р Р†Р вЂљРІР‚Сњ they explain why the layout looks the way it does.

tour.title: The tmux Bridge
tour.description: tmux_manager.py wraps libtmux: it finds the Claude Code tmux session, lists windows, captures pane content, scrapes environment and types input. Everything the bot 'sees' of an AI session comes through here Р Р†Р вЂљРІР‚Сњ it is the bottom of most dependency chains.
tour.languageLesson: A facade over an external tool (libtmux) isolates raw terminal commands behind a small API. Tests (tests/ccbot/test_tmux_manager.py) can then mock the facade instead of the real tmux daemon.

tour.title: Session Model: tmux Window Р Р†РІР‚В РІР‚в„ў Telegram Topic
tour.description: session.py is the single source of truth for the session map: it maps tmux windows to Telegram group topics and thread IDs, binds/unbinds windows, and persists the mapping. It has the highest fan-in of any src module (17 inbound edges).
tour.languageLesson: The key design decision is 1 Claude session = 1 tmux window = 1 Telegram topic. One lightweight JSON file (session map) is the persistent state; every command, notification and guard reads or writes this mapping.

tour.title: Hook Integration: How Sessions Self-Register
tour.description: Claude Code's hooks let ccbot react to events: hook.py installs a ccbot hook into Claude settings and, on SessionStart, records the live session/window mapping into the session map file with flock-protected atomic writes. session_migration.py evolves the stored format across versions.
tour.languageLesson: Claude Code exposes lifecycle hooks (SessionStart/SessionEnd) like git hooks. ccbot piggybacks on SessionStart to self-register a session instead of guessing Р Р†Р вЂљРІР‚Сњ a push-over-poll pattern that also enables session_guard to enforce authorization and topic binding.

tour.title: Command Surface & Guards
tour.description: command_handlers.py implements /start, /esc, /bind, /unbind, /status etc.; message_handlers.py handles plain-text routing; auth.py and session_guard.py enforce that only allowed users can touch bound sessions.

tour.title: Monitoring: Reading a Live Session
tour.description: session_monitor.py tails Claude's transcript JSONL in the background, terminal_parser.py decodes tmux pane content, and transcript_parser.py understands Claude session format. monitor_state.py persists per-session byte offsets so a restart resumes exactly where it left off.
tour.languageLesson: Resumable progress: instead of keeping transcripts in memory, ccbot stores the byte offset read so far on disk. That makes the monitor idempotent across restarts Р Р†Р вЂљРІР‚Сњ a durable-state trick worth reusing in any tailer/streaming feature.

tour.title: Message Fan-out: Queue, Sender & Formatting
tour.description: new session output flows into message_queue.py (per-room queuing with dedup/flood control), then message_sender.py Р Р†РІР‚В РІР‚в„ў telegram_sender.py, which chunks long messages, splits UTF-16 safely and forces Markdown-V2 escapes via markdown_v2.py; response_builder.py assembles the final Telegram entities.
tour.languageLesson: Telegram restricts bots to ~30 msg/s; a queue decouples the tmux reader from the network, letting the bot burst, dedupe and retry without dropping live output. Producer/consumer decoupling is the lesson: none of MessageQueue, MessageSender or notifications knows about tmux.

tour.title: Interactive UI: AskUserQuestion in Telegram
tour.description: Claude Code's interactive prompts (tool: AskUserQuestion) are surfaced as inline keyboards: callback_data.py encodes callbacks into compact payloads, callback_router.py dispatches them, interactive_ui.py mirrors the prompt, callback_interactive.py resolves the user's pick, callback_pickers.py builds option pickers.
tour.languageLesson: Telegram callback buttons carry only 64 bytes of callback_data, so ccbot packs compact window/session indexes and keys into payloads that stay small and serializable; tests in test_callback_data.py cover round-trip and validation.

tour.title: Notifications & Status Polling
tour.description: notifications.py fans out new messages to subscribed users and updates window offsets; status_polling.py checks tmux status lines and Claude settings to detect pending permission prompts or wait-states. These two complete the 'watch sessions at a glance' story.

tour.title: Voice & Screenshots
tour.description: transcribe.py converts incoming voice notes to text via OpenAI whisper so you can send prompts by voice; screenshot.py renders the terminal pane to an image (with a bundled CJK font via screenshot_controls.py) so you can look at the actual terminal UI.

tour.title: Foundation Utilities & Error Handling
tour.description: utils.py carries ccbot_dir() and atomic JSON writes (used by the session map and monitor state); errors.py defines the error taxonomy and message-sender error contract.
tour.languageLesson: Atomic JSON write = write to temp file (same directory), fsync, rename. Crash-safe writers avoid the classic 'half-written JSON' corruption race that would otherwise destroy the session map on power loss.

tour.title: Tests: Pin the Foundation
tour.description: The suite pins the foundation: test_session.py and test_tmux_manager.py guard the session map and the tmux facade; conftest.py shares fixtures; check.yml is the CI gate. test_utils/test_hook verify the atomic write and hook install paths.
